newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada saw continued growth, low inflation.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada saw continued growth, low inflation.

text.p: The board of directors of the Bank of Canada saw Canada's economy continuing its expansion in the months ahead, minutes from the board's meeting on March 27 released on Wednesday show.
"Altogether there were signs of increasing momentum in the pace of economic expansion and good reasons to expect a pickup in employment growth in coming months," the minutes said.
But the bank did not expect the economic growth to lead to inflation.

"The Governor (Gordon Thiessen) said that the bank expected the trend of inflation to remain under some downward pressure, within the lower part of the one to three percent inflation-control target range, in coming months," the minutes said.
The bank also said it expects economic expansion in the first quarter to strongly outpace the growth in potential output.
The country's economic growth will continue to be supported by the external economic environment, the bank said.
And the bank said growth in the M1 monetary aggregate accelerated further in January and February, "strongly suggesting that the pace of economic activity should pick up in coming quarters."
The board meeting was two days after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in over two years in an effort to stay ahead of inflation and keep economic expansion on track.
The Bank of Canada did not follow the Fed, despite pressure on the Canadian dollar at the time. The minutes did not explain why the bank made this decision.
